Attachment: feel free to drop the estimated usage CSV if you want us to plug it into our cost model. Ive attached a short draft pricing sheet with three oriented options (economy, balanced, performance) — placeholder numbers until we lock volumes.

Thanks Ana — received the CSV and ran some rough scenarios. Below is a concise set of options that map cost to latency/availability trade-offs. These are intentionally high-level; I can run model-specific numbers once you confirm the steady band you want used for projection. 

Option A — Economy (batch-first) - Target $/1M tokens: ~$600
- Typical p50 latency: 40–60ms; p95: 600–900ms (depends on batch window)
- Best for non-critical long-generation flows and background jobs
- Uses larger batching and more aggressive prefix caching
- Streaming: supported but chunks may be delayed until batch flush

Option B — Balanced (recommended for launch) - Target $/1M tokens: ~$1,800
- Typical p50: 30–40ms; p95: 250–400ms (configurable)
- Good mix of cost and responsiveness; streaming with sub-second first-byte for long outputs
- Uses adaptive batching + short batch windows for convo flows

Option C — Performance (SLO-backed) - Target $/1M tokens: ~$4,200
- Typical p50: 20–30ms; p95: <120–200ms depending on model/seq len
- Reserved dedicated capacity, strict pre-warm and cache warm policies
- Streaming is immediate and consistent; strong p95 guarantees

Notes on the numbers and mechanics:
- These are unit economics on RAW model tokens; final bill includes encoding/overhead, inference overhead (KV cache storage), and optional observability add-ons.
- If you keep steady band at 300M tokens, the monthly baseline cost estimate by option would be: A ~$180k (not recommended), B ~$540k, C ~$1.26M — but with reserved discounts and committed capacity the effective $/1M can decrease significantly (we can model 20–40% discounts for 6–12 month commits).
- Streaming vs batching trade-off: streaming reduces first byte latency but increases cost (smaller batches = lower token-efficiency). Adaptive batching (short window for conv flows, longer for background jobs) is often the best compromise.
- SLO-driven pricing: we can tie a portion of the price to guaranteed p95 targets and include fallback policies to lower-cost variants under overload. Helpful if you need strict SLAs without overpaying all the time.

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) Confirm which option (A/B/C) you want us to price against steady-state of 200M / 300M / 400M tokens. A short table from your side with a preferred baseline will help.
2) If you want to keep launch costs near your $25k/mo target, we should identify which flows can tolerate Economy (A) and which absolutely need Balanced (B).
3) I'll prepare a formal estimate and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — will include commit tiers and a starter canary plan for p95 verification.

If it helps, I'm available Wed 10/14 10–12 PT to review the sheet and walk trade-offs live.

Best — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
